newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-F.A. WRITING TO WEST HAM OVER PITCH INVASION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-F.A. WRITING TO WEST HAM OVER PITCH INVASION.

text.p: The English F.A. plan to write to West Ham in the wake of Saturday's pitch invasion by angry home spectators.
"The fans need to be aware that going on the pitch is a criminal offence," F.A. spokesman Steve Double said on Monday. "We are going to be writing to the club."
The invasion was prompted by relegation-haunted West Ham's shock F.A. Cup defeat by second division Wrexham and was the second outbreak of crowd trouble at Upton Park this season.
In December, fans rushed on to the pitch to goad Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel after captain Julian Dicks had forced and equaliser from the penalty spot.
West Ham's appalling record shows one win in 15 matches and only one goal in the last five games.
To add to the fans frustrations the West Ham board have yet to make a decision on Michael Tabor's 30 million pounds ($48.7 million) takeover bid.
Tabor had threatened to withdraw the offer if the board did not meet to discuss it by last Friday.
Tabor, a big West Ham supporter, has made repeated bids for the club, but the former bookmaker has been frustrated by the board's lack of interest.

West Ham managing director Peter Storrie said money would be made available to manager Harry Redknapp to buy some much needed attacking players. Redknapp had offered to quit following Saturday's defeat.
